title: The model's biggest well-sampled miss: late-inning long shots
headline_insight: Late in MLB games, a team the model gives 0.262 to win actually wins 0.0843 of the time -- a 0.1778 calibration error and the model's largest miss in any cell with n over 500 (n=617).
what_it_means: This exhibit buckets every graded in-game prediction by confidence band and game phase to find where the model drifts furthest from reality. On the segment-clean corpus the worst well-sampled cells are low-probability bands, where the model leaves too much hope on teams that are already beaten. The late-inning heavy-favorite cell that revision 1 called the biggest miss is now close to honest: the model says 0.9101 and those teams win 0.9498, a 0.0397 error over 2,369 rows. Tinier buckets look far worse but rest on almost no data.
how_to_read: Each row is a (game-phase x probability band) cell; calibration_error is the absolute distance between what the model said (mean_p) and what happened (mean_y).
why_it_matters: It is a ranked improvement backlog -- it names the exact game states to fix first, weighted by how much data backs each miss.
caveat: The very worst rows in ranked_worst_buckets have tiny n (the top one, calibration_error 0.7892, is only n=7) and are noise-dominated; the n-weighted ECE summary (mlb model 0.0494 vs market 0.0397) is the stable read.
